Committee: Governmental Affairs
Sponsor: Allen
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 04/02/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 358 as introduced would prohibit the state and any political subdivision, and any appointed or elected official in the state from enforcing any federal act, law, order, rule, or regulation that regulates the possession, use, or manufacture of any firearm, ammunition, or firearm accessory and imposes penalties for violations under certain circumstances. This bill could increase the obligations of the Office of Attorney General, by an undetermined amount, to: (1) seek action against any political subdivision in the state for violations of this bill as a result of a valid compliant filed by a resident of that political subdivision; this increase would be offset by a court award for reasonable expenses; and (2) defend any resident against federal allegations of violations of federal laws or regulations relating to the manufacture, sale, transfer, or possession of firearms ammunition, or firearm accessories. This bill could also decrease state grant revenues to any political subdivision of the state that violates this bill by an undetermined amount.
In addition this bill could increase receipts to the State General Fund and municipal general funds from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, and local jails by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by this bill and the penalties imposed.
Jimmy Holley, Chairperson
Governmental Affairs

Committee: Transportation, Utilities and Infrastructure
Sponsor: Orr
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 03/12/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 211 as passed the Senate provides that all-terrain and off-highway vehicle registration fees currently required to be deposited into an off-road vehicle account in the State Treasury for certain uses would now be deposited into the Public Safety Fund of the Alabama Law Enforcement Agency (ALEA). According to ALEA, approximately $250 in registration fees have been deposited for Fiscal Year 2021 year-to-date.
Lynn Greer, Chair
Transportation, Utilities and Infrastructure

Committee: Governmental Affairs
Sponsor: Orr
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 02/24/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 211 as introduced will not affect state or local funding.
As substituted and reported by the Committee on Governmental Affairs would increase receipts deposited into the Public Safety Fund of the Alabama Law Enforcement Agency by a small undetermined amount from registration fees currently collected for all-terrain and off-highway vehicles that are currently required to be deposited into an off-road vehicle account in the State Treasury and used for the acquisition of off-road trail and use areas, and to fund a grant in-aid program to counties and municipalities for the same.
Jimmy Holley, Chairperson
Governmental Affairs

Committee: Public Safety and Homeland Security
Sponsor: Allen
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 04/26/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 358 as passed the Senate would prohibit the state and any political subdivision, and any appointed or elected official in the state from enforcing any federal act, law, order, rule, or regulation that regulates the possession, use, or manufacture of any firearm, ammunition, or firearm accessory and imposes penalties for violations under certain circumstances. This bill could increase the obligations of the Office of Attorney General, by an undetermined amount, to: (1) seek action against any political subdivision in the state for violations of this bill as a result of a valid compliant filed by a resident of that political subdivision; this increase would be offset by a court award for reasonable expenses; and (2) defend any resident against federal allegations of violations of federal laws or regulations relating to the manufacture, sale, transfer, or possession of firearms ammunition, or firearm accessories. This bill could also decrease state grant revenues to any political subdivision of the state that violates this bill by an undetermined amount dependent on the grant revenues otherwise received by the political subdivision.
In addition this bill could increase receipts to the State General Fund and municipal general funds from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, and local jails by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by this bill and the penalties imposed.
Allen Treadaway, Chair
Public Safety and Homeland Security

Committee: Public Safety and Homeland Security
Sponsor: Allen
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 04/27/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 358 as substituted and reported by the Committee on Public Safety and Homeland Security would prohibit the state and any political subdivision, and any appointed or elected official, officer, or employee from enforcing any Presidential Executive Orders, effective after January 1, 2021, that would regulate the ownership, possession, or use of firearms, ammunition, or firearm accessories of law-aiding residents of the state.
This bill could increase the administrative obligations of the Office of the Attorney General to provide guidance to state and local officials on complying with the provisions of this bill.
Allen Treadaway, Chair
Public Safety and Homeland Security
